parsed.why: Governor's order backs single-sex facilities in state buildings, surgery-gated markers, under-19 care ban, and documented birth-sex custody placement where a court dismissed failure-to-protect after sexual assault. Statewide gender-identity protections absent; national law covers bias crimes only.

Only jurisdiction criminalising trans restroom/changing-room use in private businesses — gas stations, restaurants, hospitals — misdemeanour up to a year; remedy is pending litigation, not operating. State-imposed universal exposure with criminal penalty, deepest in the set.

Facility law is school/college only with no enforcement mechanism or penalty, so it barely reaches a visitor; care and sports bans are resident-facing and enjoined. No public-accommodation criminal ban, but marker rules tightened and protections patchy.

No facility ban reaching visitors; exposures are resident-facing (under-18 care ban, one city's surgical suspension) plus a city cluster of trans-woman homicides reported as raw counts without a denominator — background violence, not a documented campaign.

No bathroom ban of its own and rated low-risk in the 2026 assessment; the facility restriction is a national-legislature override with arrests at the legislature, and federal override power limits durability but adds no visitor-specific facility or custody exposure.
